chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both)

Regarding the concubine (slave woman) whom a man marries: he said, 'No, and even if she is his slave, and even if he wishes to have sexual relations with her, he does not make her an Umm al-Walad (mother of the child who gains freedom upon the master's death).'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of the child (a slave woman who bears her master's child and gains partial freedom upon his death)
key_terms.وَطِئَهَا: To have sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: Does marrying a slave woman make her an Umm al-Walad in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from the chapter on slave women clarifies that a master's marriage to his own slave woman does not automatically elevate her to the status of *Umm al-Walad* (mother of the child) upon bearing offspring. This ruling highlights the distinct legal categories in Shia jurisprudence, where *Umm al-Walad* status is contingent upon specific conditions rather than mere marital union, ensuring her continued servitude until explicitly freed or the child's birth triggers emancipation under different interpretations.
